spec.name: odin-landing-lead
spec.type: Landing page with lead-capture contact form
spec.stack: Next.js (App Router, React, TypeScript) fullstack with API routes + Prisma ORM over PostgreSQL; deployed to the Azure VM (django-vm, resource group DJANGO-PROJECT) behind the existing nginx/systemd setup, ports 80/443 kept open
spec.description: Build a SMALL landing page with a contact form that saves leads to a database — this is run 'rep 1'. Deploy it when finished. The owner explicitly said: NO QA agent for this project. Objective: a single responsive landing page (hero + copy + CTA) containing a contact form (typical fields: name, email, message) that persists each submission as a lead row in a PostgreSQL database via a Next.js API route backed by Prisma, with server-side validation and a success/error state on submit. Platform/stack: Next.js + TypeScript fullstack (UI + API routes in one app), Prisma + PostgreSQL for the leads table. All work is done INSIDE the project's own folder (to be created under the workspace projects dir, e.g. workspace/projects/odin-landing-lead), never at the Odin repo root. Deploy step: once built and verified locally, deploy to the Azure VM — firewall rotated to the owner's current IP on port 22 only (80/443 stay open), rsync as user mostafa (excluding secrets/.env*/keys/backups), run prisma migrate deploy (additive only, never reset), build, and restart via systemd; then confirm it is online. Explicit owner constraints kept verbatim: 'Build a small landing page with a contact form that saves leads to a database (rep 1), deploy it when finished. No QA agent for this project.'
features: Responsive landing page (hero, value copy, CTA)
Contact form with fields (name, email, message)
Client-side + server-side validation of form input
Next.js API route that receives the submission
Persist each submission as a lead record in PostgreSQL via Prisma
Success / error feedback states on the form
Production deploy to the Azure VM with service restart and online health check

features.name: Spam protection (honeypot or rate limit)
features.why: A public contact form will attract bot submissions; a lightweight honeypot/rate-limit keeps the leads table clean without adding a captcha dependency.

features.name: Lead notification (email/HubSpot)
features.why: Pushing new leads to email or HubSpot (already connected) means the owner acts on leads immediately instead of polling the DB.

members.name: Designer
members.why: A landing page's conversion depends on visual polish; a Designer would sharpen layout/branding, but Fullstack can ship a clean standard design without one — owner's call.
